en: Never enter Mayon Volcano's Permanent Danger Zone to protect yourself from deadly pyroclastic flows and sudden lava eruptions.
Monitor PAGASA's Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals to know when to evacuate and prepare emergency kits before a typhoon.
Avoid swimming in the Cagayan River during heavy rains because sudden flash floods can sweep people away.
Evacuate to higher ground immediately if you feel a strong earthquake near the Davao Gulf coast to avoid tsunamis.
Eliminate stagnant water around your Metro Manila home to stop mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dangerous dengue fever.
Enjoy Baguio City's high elevation and cool climate to prevent heat exhaustion during outdoor sports and activities.
Swim only between the red and yellow flags at La Union beaches to avoid dangerous underwater rip currents.
Check if your Metro Manila school or home is far from the Valley Fault System to stay safe from earthquakes.
Wear an N95 mask during a Taal Volcano ashfall to protect your lungs from inhaling hazardous volcanic particles.
Always boil tap water after a typhoon flood in low-lying Manila areas to prevent dangerous waterborne diseases.
Avoid hiking steep Cordillera mountain trails during the rainy season to prevent accidents caused by deadly mudslides.
Wear protective rash guards while snorkeling in Palawan's coral reefs to prevent painful jellyfish stings and severe sunburns.
